# ar/

## Modules
- **Quote → invoice pipeline**: `quoteService.ts`, `quoteConvertService.ts`, `quotePdfBuilder.ts`; `salesOrderService.ts`, `salesOrderWorkflowService.ts`; `deliveryNoteService.ts`.
- **Customer invoices / credit notes**: `invoicePdfService.ts` (facade), `invoicePdfBuilder.ts`, `invoicePdfSnapshotService.ts` (PRD-06 sealed PDF evidence), `creditNoteService.ts`, `creditNotePdfBuilder.ts`.
- **Payments + write-offs**: `customerPaymentService.ts`, `customerPaymentAllocationService.ts` (confirm/cancel use ALS-bound `sql`), `writeOffService.ts`, `receiptMatchService.ts`, `readReceiptService.ts`.
- **Recurring + collections**: `recurringInvoiceService.ts`, `smartCollectionsService.ts` (pure tone/escalation), `arAgingService.ts`, `debtorsManagerService.ts`.
- **Subledger snapshot (point-in-time)**: `arSubledgerService.ts`, `subledgerShared.ts`, `subledgerTypes.ts` — every open customer document as at a date, on the SAME population and the SAME settlement rewind (`shared/agingRewind.ts`) as `arAgingService`. Consumed by `services/reconciliation/`. Two populations would make `reconcile_subledger`'s aged-versus-subledger comparison meaningless, so do not diverge them.
- **Dunning (PRD-06 Phase 5)**: `dunningService.ts` (render), `dunningSend.ts` (send), `dunningCronService.ts`, `dunningAdmin.ts`, `dunningDefaults.ts`, `dunningOverridesService.ts`, `dunningInboundParseService.ts`.
- **Sent-folder mirror (PRD-06 Phase 6)**: `sentMirrorService.ts`, `sentMirrorAdmin.ts`.
- **Disputes (PRD-06 Phase 3)**: `disputeService.ts` (raise/list/get), `disputeResolution.ts` (resolve/withdraw), `disputeTypes.ts` (shared types + `mapRow`).
- **Customer merge**: `customerMergeService.ts` — `mergeCustomers(companyId, sourceId, targetId)`, the ONE merge behind both `customer-merge` and `duplicates-merge` (K-061).
- **Typed request errors**: `arErrors.ts` — `ArRequestError(message, status, code)`. The ONLY thing an AR route may answer with a 4xx.
- **Statements**: `statementEmailService.ts`, `statementEmailTypes.ts`, `statementEmailTemplate.ts`.
- **Customer portal**: `portalService.ts` (bcrypt auth, separate from GoTrue), `portalSession.ts` (the one `portal_session` resolver), `portalChatbotService.ts`, `portalTokenService.ts`, `portalLinkCharge.ts` (what a payment link may charge; spending it on settlement); `gatewayInvoiceReceiptService.ts` + `gatewaySettlementReview.ts` + `gatewayReceiptAllocation.ts` (banking a Paystack settlement; what it banks, when it is flagged, and how much the invoice takes under its row lock).
- `index.ts` — barrel (conflicting symbol files listed in header).

## Caller contract
Invoked by `withCompany`-wrapped API routes in `pages/api/accounting/ar/*` and `pages/api/portal/*`. Every public DB function takes `companyId` first (portal functions additionally verify `client_id` against the calling company).

## Main function signatures
- `createQuote(companyId, input, userId?) / updateQuoteStatus / convertQuoteToInvoice`.
- `createCustomerPayment(companyId, input)`; `confirmCustomerPayment(companyId, id, userId)` — GL: DR Bank, CR AR; updates invoice balances atomically. `cancelCustomerPayment` — reverses JE.
- `raiseDispute / resolveDispute / withdrawDispute / getOpenDisputeTotals(companyId)`.
- `loadInvoiceCtx(companyId, invoiceId)`, `renderTemplate(tpl, ctx)`, `sendDunning(input)` — inserts immutable `dunning_sends` row with rendered subject/body.
- `scanAllDueSentConnections()` — cron tick; `scanSentConnection(conn)` — IMAP pull.
- `authenticatePortalUser(email, password)`, `getClientInvoices(clientId, companyId)`, `createPaymentLink(invoiceId, clientId, amount)`.

## Business rules
- **Lock order**: the canonical sequence for every settlement path (bank line → payment → invoices → GL) lives in `bank/.claude.md`. Read it before adding a lock here; a path that takes two of these rows out of sequence deadlocks against one that does not (40P01 → 500).

- `customer_invoices.status`: `draft | sent | partial | paid | void | written_off`. All AR invoice queries MUST use `COALESCE(ci.client_id, ci.customer_id)` — both columns exist (legacy mig artefact).
- Confirm/cancel-payment uses ALS-bound `sql` (NOT `withTransaction`) — the outer `withAuth` transaction provides atomicity. Using `withTransaction` here caused idle-in-transaction timeouts because it opened a second pool connection while the ALS client sat idle.
- 2026-04-24: JE link-back uses ALS-bound `sql` instead of `withTransaction` to avoid nested-tx issues. Do NOT pass invoice id as JE `sourceDocumentId` (FK is to `documents`).
- Dunning: render applies `{{token}}` substitution; send writes an immutable row (subject/body frozen for audit).
- Dispute state: `open → resolved | rejected | withdrawn`. Re-raising after resolution creates a NEW row — history preserved.
- Portal auth is bcrypt against `portal_users` — never route portal endpoints through the main `withAuth` middleware.
- PRD-06 Phase 1: invoice-as-evidence — sealed PDF snapshot is persisted on approve/send for audit.
- `smartCollectionsService` is pure; R50 000 threshold is hard-coded (not per-company).
- **`fetchInvoiceCandidates` (`receiptAllocationLines`) LOCKS the invoices it decides from** — `ORDER BY ci.id`, `FOR UPDATE OF ci`, 5s `lock_timeout`, 55P03 → `ReceiptRefusal`. It THROWS outside a request transaction rather than skipping the lock (`core/requestTransaction`): an implicit transaction releases `FOR UPDATE` at the end of the statement and discards the `SET LOCAL lock_timeout`, so the check-then-act ran unprotected and unbounded while reading as locked. `lock_timeout` is restored on the SUCCESS path only — a `finally` would raise 25P02 over the refusal. `ap/fetchBillCandidates` is the mirror.
- `recurringInvoiceService.generateInvoiceFromRecurring` inserts the invoice at `draft`, writes one
  `customer_invoice_items` row per template line, then approves it through `approveCustomerInvoice`
  — so it DOES post the GL journal. Never post again on top of it. It requires a request
  transaction (`FOR UPDATE` on the template), refuses a template that is not yet due, and derives
  the header totals from the lines rather than the stored aggregate. The savepoint opens BEFORE the
  lock: the 5s `lock_timeout` raises 55P03, which aborts the whole request transaction, and outside
  a savepoint that silently turns the batch runner's COMMIT into a ROLLBACK. `assertTxUsable` does
  NOT see this — `txUnusable` is set only when a savepoint's own rollback fails.

## Recent changes
- 2026-10-02 (R-181): **Paystack settlement** — `recordGatewayInvoiceReceipt`; the webhook and `verify` both settle through it, idempotent on the reference (`docs/audits/remediation/R-181/fix.md`).
  - **Banked:** `requested_amount` when `0 <= amount - requested_amount <= fees` (the excess is a fee the customer paid); otherwise `amount`; with no `amount`, `requested_amount`; with neither, the request's `amount_cents` (`gatewaySettlementReview.settledCharge`).
  - **Allocated:** decided under the invoice row lock (`gatewayReceiptAllocation.decideGatewayAllocation`, arithmetic in the pure `allocationPlan`): `min(banked, total_amount - amount_paid - draft receipts' open allocations against the invoice)`. NOTHING when the invoice is outside the ledger (draft, pending_approval, cancelled, soft-deleted), the charge is not ZAR, or the balance is not a finite number; the rest is an unapplied receipt on the customer, re-read under the lock (a merge moves it).
  - **Fee leg:** `fees - (amount - banked)`, clamped to `[0, fees]` and never above the receipt (`merchantFee`); any whole cent posts; posted once per reference (`postGatewayFee`, reference + posting agent) by whichever of webhook and verify carries `fees` first; never for a non-ZAR charge.
  - **Not flagged (pre-existing, warn only):** `postGatewayFee` skips the fee leg with a `log.warn` when the receipt has no bank account or no `admin_expense` system account resolves; Bank then stays above the deposit by the fee and the request carries no review reason. Every other case where Bank cannot reach Paystack's settlement is flagged.
  - **Second report:** banks nothing; posts a missing fee against what the FIRST report banked; flags its own reasons, plus `amount_disagrees_with_first_report` when its bank figure or Paystack's `amount` differs from the first report's (a first `amount` that differs from the receipt is tagged in the receipt description).
  - **verify's answer:** `amountCents` = the receipt's total once banked, `appliedToInvoice`, and `currency` (the receipt's reported currency, from its description tag via `receiptCurrency`); the return page shows a rand figure only for ZAR.
  - **Flagged:** `paystack_payment_requests.failure_reason = 'review:<reasons>'` and `log.error`. Reasons: `amount_not_reported`, `amount_mismatch`, `amount_below_requested_amount`, `requested_amount_exceeds_fee`, `requested_amount_unverified`, `currency_mismatch`, `unapplied_currency`, `invoice_<status>`, `invoice_deleted`, `invoice_balance_invalid`, `overpaid_unapplied`, `fee_not_posted_currency`, `fee_clamped`, `fee_exceeds_receipt`, `amount_disagrees_with_first_report`. Notes merge; a prior non-review reason is kept after ` | previously: `. Written in its own savepoint: a failed write is logged and never costs the receipt. No UI shows the flag (Hein).
  - **Lock order:** request row (webhook/verify UPDATE) → explicit-amount `portal_payment_links` row (`spendPaymentLinkOfRequest`) → the receipt's own new `customer_payments` row → the invoice (`withCustomerInvoiceLock`, 5s). On the DEDUPE path (receipt already banked) there is no request UPDATE: spend link → fee journal (`postGatewayFee`) → the request row `FOR UPDATE` last (the review note), with no `lock_timeout`; no cycle, because the request is already completed and nothing that holds it waits on the link or a journal. `customerMergeService` takes invoice → link, the opposite, so a merge racing the settlement of the same customer's explicit-amount link can raise 40P01 (pre-existing; recoverable: the webhook answers 500 and is redelivered, the merge errors and is retried). The one exception to "no payment lock while holding an invoice lock": confirmCustomerPayment locks the settlement's OWN new, uncommitted payment row while the invoice is held; that is safe because the row is invisible to every other transaction, so nothing can hold it or wait on it. Any settlement failure rolls back: the webhook answers 500 for redelivery; `verify` answers `pending` when Paystack said success, or when Paystack never answered on a request stored `failed` (never `failed` unless Paystack said so), and leaves the request as it was stored for the webhook.

(3) **`agingRewind` reads the ALLOCATION ROWS, not the link column.** Rewinding `applied_amount` against the one invoice a note names credits back money taken off a different one the moment a note spreads. (Its `creditsCancelled` fragment is inert and always was — cancel zeroes `applied_amount` in the same statement — and is now labelled so.) (4) **THE DOCUMENTS ARE LOCKED BEFORE THE PLAN IS MADE.** `creditNoteApplicationWrites.lockInvoicesForUpdate` takes one `FOR UPDATE` over every candidate ORDERED BY id, and the plan consumes THOSE balances — planning from the candidate query's figures let two notes approved concurrently against one 1,000 invoice both plan against 1,000 and drive `amount_paid` to 1,300 (proved, and proved again by mutation, in `tests/integration/l2-credit-note-fifo.int.test.ts`). The id order is what keeps two overlapping batches off a deadlock, and the bounded helper is what stops an unbounded wait turning one stuck request into two. NOTE the end-to-end approval cannot be raced in a test: journal numbering collides on `uq_gl_je_company_entry_number` first, which is a separate pre-existing defect. (5) **`applied_amount` must equal the SUM of the rows**, and both the apply and the cancel paths refuse when it does not (`assertAllocationsMatchApplied`). The shape that breaks it is reachable: a pre-677 note with no link that the backfill could not attribute carries a figure no row explains, and extending it would strand the original credit. There is no safe automatic repair, so it is named and refused. (6) **A LINKED document that has posted nothing is SKIPPED, not credited and not refused.** The link is validated at create time, but the document can be cancelled or taken back to draft before the note is approved; crediting it would move a balance the ledger no longer carries, and refusing the whole approval would strand a real credit as a draft. The walk takes the money instead. (7) **A legacy note with `applied_amount > 0` and NO allocation rows cannot be extended at all** — applying it again would write a row for the new amount only and leave the note permanently uncancellable, so it is refused by name. Cancelling one is still safe: the cancel path sees no rows and falls back to its single link. (8) **`credit_note_allocations` is under RLS (migration 678, applied separately because 677 was already applied and an applied migration is never edited).** ENABLE + FORCE + `tenant_isolation` FOR ALL TO app_user, the same four statements every other tenant table uses. It matters more here than the shape suggests: `invoice_id` is deliberately NOT a foreign key — it points at `customer_invoices` or `supplier_invoices` depending on the note's type — so nothing else constrains which document a row may name, and `cancelCreditNote` READS these rows to hand money back. A forged row is an instruction to reduce a stranger's `amount_paid`. Verified as `app_user`, not inferred: a foreign row is invisible, forging one raises `new row violates row-level security policy`, deleting one affects nothing, and the tenant's own write reads back once `request.jwt.claims` is set — the USING clause reads `auth.uid()` through it, so the company GUC alone is not enough. (9) **`auto_apply: 'none'`** keeps the old behaviour and is REFUSED rather than coerced when it is neither value, on the MCP tools and the REST routes alike: coercing a typo to the default spends credit the caller asked to keep on account.
- 2026-09-18 (L1 r2): the open-invoice fetch moved to `openCustomerInvoices.ts` with the same `{ forUpdate }` option as the AP twin — `autoApplyCustomerReceipt` locks, the bulk `dry_run` preview does not. `customerAutoAllocate` re-exports it.
- 2026-09-18 (L1): **the AR twin of the FIFO default.** `autoApplyCustomerReceipt` takes the same `autoApply` mode, `fetchOpenCustomerInvoices` locks with `FOR UPDATE OF ci`, skips soft-deleted rows and orders `ci.invoice_date ASC, ci.due_date ASC NULLS LAST, ci.id ASC`. Its unallocatable-status list names `'disputed'` and `'written_off'` although `customer_invoices`' CHECK constraint carries neither (a dispute lives in `customer_invoice_disputes`) — the two lists are kept identical deliberately, because two subledgers disagreeing about what cash may settle is how they drift apart. `recomputeInvoiceStatus` is now the ONLY writer of `supplier_invoices.payment_matched`; see `capture/.claude.md`.
- 2026-09-18: **statementEmailService's running balance and totals now accumulate in decimal** (`@/lib/money/decimalSum.ts`), not JS float — `let running = 0; running += debit - credit` over a long transaction list drifted into payloads like `126629.94999999995` and `-4.3655745685100555e-11`. Every money field (`debit`/`credit`/`balance`, `excluded[].amount`, `summary.*`) is rounded to 2dp via `toMoney` before it leaves the service (L4).
- 2026-09-09: **both remaining convert paths claim before they mint (K-121 r4).** `quoteConvertService.convertToInvoice` read `quote.status !== 'accepted'` and then minted, and `salesOrderWorkflowService.convertSalesOrderToInvoice` read `order.status !== 'confirmed'` and then minted — check-then-act on both, so two concurrent requests (two tabs, a retry, the API called directly) each reserved a number and each inserted a full invoice with the source document's lines: the customer billed twice, AR and output VAT overstated, and `converted_invoice_id` / `invoice_id` pointing at only one of the two, so the duplicate is invisible from the quote or order. The counter row lock serialises the NUMBERING and does not stop this. Both now take a status-predicated claiming `UPDATE ... RETURNING id` BEFORE the sequence is touched, and the loser re-reads and throws `QuoteNotInvoiceableError` / `SalesOrderNotInvoiceableError` carrying the winner's invoice id, which the routes answer 409 (previously 400 for the status refusal; a missing quote is now 404). `customer-sales-orders-action` also caught everything into `badRequestFromError` — a 4xx after a write, which `withAuth` COMMITs — and now maps only those pre-write refusals and rethrows the rest.
- 2026-09-09: **A 4xx is a COMMIT — so a route may never decide one from an error MESSAGE.** `withAuth` COMMITs on any status below 500. The resolve route matched `/not found/i` and answered 400; `createCreditNote` throws the bare literal `'Not found'` when a link target is gone (a soft-deleted customer is enough); and the claim UPDATE now runs BEFORE the credit note. So a missing customer left the dispute permanently `resolved` with `credit_note_id` NULL, no note behind it, and no retry — the claim predicate wants `status = 'open'`. Two rules come out of it. (1) **Errors are typed, never text-matched**: `ArRequestError` (`arErrors.ts`) marks a deliberate, caller-correctable refusal the service raises itself; every AR dispute/dunning route now classifies on `instanceof` and rethrows everything else, so an unexpected failure reaches `withAuth` as a 5xx and ROLLBACKs. (2) **A claim and the document it claims for share one savepoint**: `resolveDispute` wraps claim + `createCreditNote` + link in `withSavepoint('dispute_resolve')`, so even a legitimate 400 raised after the claim (an invoice with no client, an invoice whose amounts admit no VAT rate) unwinds it. Proved by outcome in `tests/integration/k122e-…` on a real transaction. Also: `sendEmail`'s `email_log` INSERT is now AWAITED and inside `withSavepoint('email_log_write')` — it ran on the caller's transaction between the dispatch and the `dunning_sends.email_status` UPDATE, so its failure aborted the transaction and lost the record of an email already delivered (`k122f-…`). And the credit note's `tax_rate` is the invoice's own rate whenever that reconciles with its amounts; only a genuinely mixed-rate invoice gets a blended figure, which is logged as derived, and a positive tax over a non-positive subtotal is refused rather than booked at 0%.
- 2026-09-09: **Dispute resolution, the dunning skip gate, and the send/evidence ordering.** (1) `resolveDispute` CLAIMS the dispute with one status-predicated `UPDATE … WHERE status = 'open' RETURNING` **before** it calls `createCreditNote`. A read-then-write let two concurrent resolves both see `open`, both raise a credit note for the same disputed amount, and the second UPDATE overwrite `credit_note_id` — one real financial document left orphaned. Claim first, create the document second, link it third; never the other way round. (2) Resolving "with credit" leaves a **draft** credit note: nothing posts to the GL and nothing is applied to the invoice, so the amount is still in overdue. The dunning cron therefore skips an invoice whose dispute is `open` **or** whose dispute carries a credit note still in `draft` (`has_blocking_dispute`), and resumes once it is approved. Closing a dispute is not the same as crediting it. (3) `sendDunning` records `email_status` immediately after `sendEmail` and seals its `captured_documents` evidence row in its OWN savepoint with the failure logged, not thrown. Everything after the dispatch runs inside the cron's per-invoice savepoint, so a rollback there would erase the `dunning_sends` row while the customer keeps the email — and the cron's "no existing send" gate would re-send the same escalation the next morning. It also refuses outright to email a body still carrying `PORTAL_LINK_UNAVAILABLE`. (4) `createCreditNote` accepts an exact `taxAmount`: rounding subtotal and tax independently leaves `subtotal + tax` a cent off a known VAT-inclusive gross (10.00 at 15% → 8.70 + 1.31), and no split of that gross is exact, so the caller that knows the gross passes the remainder.
- 2026-09-09: **Dunning portal links, and three things that are easy to get wrong again.** (1) `renderTemplate` now issues SQL, so it can raise inside the request transaction. Its mint is deliberately NOT wrapped in try/catch — `withAuth` runs the whole handler in ONE transaction, so a swallowed PG error aborts it and every later statement (the `dunning_sends` and `captured_documents` INSERTs) fails with 25P02; a caller that did survive would email the customer `(portal link unavailable)` and record it as `sent`. **Catching is not isolation.** `dunningCronService` wraps each invoice in `withSavepoint('dunning_cron_invoice')` so one transient lock rolls back to its own savepoint instead of failing every remaining invoice in the run. (2) `getOrMintInvoicePortalToken` mints with `UPDATE … SET portal_token = COALESCE(portal_token, $1) … RETURNING`, never a read-modify-write: the cron and a manual send can render the same invoice concurrently, and the loser of a read-then-write emails a token that is not in the database — the exact 404 the token exists to remove. Use the read-only `getInvoicePortalToken` on any path that only DISPLAYS a link (preview): the token is a permanent unauthenticated credential and `withAuth` COMMITs on 4xx, so a read-shaped request must not persist one. (3) `resolveDispute` derives the credit note's `taxRate` from the invoice — `disputed_amount` is a slice of the VAT-INCLUSIVE total and `createCreditNote` expects a VAT-EXCLUSIVE subtotal, so a flat `taxRate: 0` books the whole amount to revenue and nothing to VAT output. `customer_invoices.amount_paid` is NULLABLE: every `total_amount - amount_paid` needs `COALESCE(…, 0)` or the row silently drops out of a `> 0` filter and contributes NULL to a SUM (fixed in AR aging, AFS receivables/payables notes, custom-report balances and bank-match ordering).
- 2026-09-09: **`customer_invoices` row locks — `customerInvoiceLock.ts`, and the two paths that write `amount_paid`.** Both writers used to compute their cap from an UNLOCKED read and then write the money. `applyCreditNoteToInvoice` also wrote `amount_paid` ABSOLUTELY from that stale read, so a second credit note or a receipt committing in between was erased outright; `planAllocationLines` writes relatively but its `outstanding` cap was equally stale, so a receipt planned against R200 landed its full R200 on top of a credit note's R100 and left R300 on a R200 invoice. Both now take `FOR UPDATE` and the credit-note write is relative. **The lock ORDER is note-then-invoice / payment-then-invoice / bank-line-then-invoice.** (Not "the invoice is last" — `customerInvoiceCancelService` holds an invoice and then locks `gl_journal_entries`; that stays acyclic because the only path holding a journal row when it reaches an invoice is `cancelCreditNote`, and the journal it holds is the NOTE's.) Reversing the order above anywhere deadlocks (40P01, which surfaces as GENERIC_FAILURE and does not read as retryable to an agent), so never take a credit-note or payment lock while holding an invoice one. `planAllocationLines` orders its candidates `ORDER BY ci.id` for the same reason across rows. `withCustomerInvoiceLock` carries the 5s `lock_timeout` and the typed `CustomerInvoiceLockTimeoutError`, restoring `DEFAULT` on the SUCCESS PATH ONLY — same rule and same reasons as `creditNoteLock.ts`. **Closed 2026-09-18 — see the top entry.** approval credits AR for a note's FULL `total_amount` while `applyCreditNoteToInvoice` caps at the invoice's outstanding and then marks the note `applied`, so a partial application strands the remainder and the GL diverges from the subledger by it. `credit_notes` carries ONE `customer_invoice_id`, which is also how cancel un-applies, so spreading a note over two invoices needs a link table — not fixable in place.
- 2026-09-09: **Soft-deleted invoices leave AR aging, the AR subledger snapshot, dunning and the customer statement** (audit K-053). `deleted_at` was filtered by `customerLedgerService` and by nothing else, so a deleted invoice kept a balance in `getARAging`/`getARAgingDetail`, in `arSubledgerService` and in every chase surface. Two things worth not re-deriving. (1) **Aging and the subledger snapshot must gain the predicate together** — they are required to run on one population, and adding it to aging alone made `reconcile_subledger` report the deleted amount as an unexplained residual. (2) **The GL has to move with them**: soft-delete previously left the approval journal posted, so filtering the document alone would have broken the tie to the control account. `core/softDeleteJournalService` now reverses that journal on delete and re-instates it on undo, through the canonical `reverseJournalEntry`, and a delete is refused when payments exist or the reversal's period is closed. (3) **The exclusion is DATED, because the reversal is** (round 4). `reverseJournalEntry` dates the reversal to the original entry date only while that period is open and otherwise to TODAY, so for a document raised in a closed prior month — the ordinary case — the control account keeps carrying it right up to the delete. An undated `deleted_at IS NULL` therefore measures the two sides of an as-at comparison on different clocks: `arSubLedgerCheck` failed by the whole document amount for every period between the invoice and the delete. `shared/softDeleteLedgerPresence.documentInLedgerAsAtFragment` answers the dated question by the reversal chain's PARITY as at the date (odd = standing), which also covers documents deleted BEFORE this change, whose journal is still posted, with no historical repair. It must be paired with a GL half bounded by `entry_date <= <as-at>`, and it is interpolation-only — the return is a thenable, so awaiting it sends the bare fragment to Postgres as a statement. Its PRECONDITION is that no reversal is dated before the entry it reverses (`resolveReversalDate`); parity only equals the net position when the entries `<= as-at` form a prefix of the chain. Round 5 carried the same dated predicate into the as-at CHASE surfaces — `statementEmailService` and `pages/api/accounting/customer-statement` — which had kept an undated `deleted_at IS NULL` and so stated a balance to the customer that disagreed with both aging and the GL at every date before the delete. The undated predicate is still correct in `dunningService`, `dunningCronService` and `smart-reminder`, which chase as at NOW and never take an as-at date. Round 6 closed the census the round-5 change left open: `customerLedgerService` is the sixth as-at surface — the AR mirror of `reports-supplier-ledger`, taking `dateFrom`/`dateTo` on the document the customer is asked to pay — and it kept the undated `deleted_at IS NULL OR deleted_at > NOW()` on BOTH legs, so after round 5 it disagreed with the emailed statement AND with the GL by the whole document for every window ending before the delete. Both legs now take the fragment at `dateTo ?? today`, and note that the OPENING leg is dated to `dateTo`, NOT to `dateFrom`: the ledger lists documents and never the GL reversal the delete posts, so a delete inside the window produces no row, and an opening dated to `dateFrom` would carry an invoice that nothing in the window then removes. The dead `OR deleted_at > NOW()` disjunct is gone with it — no writer sets `deleted_at` to a future time. Round 6 also stopped `statementEmailService` and `customer-statement` drawing a statement for a soft-deleted CUSTOMER, and gave `customer-statement` the `COALESCE(ci.client_id, ci.customer_id)` form the emailed statement already used.
- 2026-09-03: **Cash application — `receiptApplicationService` + `receiptAllocationLines` + `receiptMatchConfirmService` + `unappliedReceiptService`/`unappliedReceiptOrigin`.** `allocateTransaction(allocType='customer')` posts DR Bank / CR AR and inserts a CONFIRMED `customer_payments` row, then writes NO `customer_payment_allocations` and never touches `amount_paid` — the cash sits on the control account attached to no document. Re-derived against production 2026-09-03: **R42,759,565.12 unapplied system-wide, of which R39,486,371.68 (92.3%) carries an `mcp:` posting stamp and every one is `bulk_allocate_bank_transactions`** (Velocity Fibre's R37,050,347.68 is 100% agent-made). The bucket is FILLED BY THE TOOLING, not historical. Four things worth not re-deriving. (1) **PLAN and APPLY are separate functions over ONE set of guards.** `planReceiptApplication` takes the `FOR UPDATE` lock (`core/paymentLock.ts`), runs every guard, writes nothing; `applyReceiptPlan` writes and guards nothing. A dry run is the first without the second, so it cannot pass where the live call refuses — and every refusal can be answered before the first write, which is what both the MCP idempotency contract and `withAuth`'s COMMIT-under-500 rule require. (2) **`COALESCE(ci.client_id, ci.customer_id)` is the counterparty.** The inline SQL in `customer-allocations.ts` compared `client_id` alone, so an invoice populated on `customer_id` had `client_id` NULL and could never be allocated through the only UI path that exists — a plausible direct cause of the receipts never being applied. That route also wrote `amount_paid` absolutely (lost update), returned `badRequest` from inside its write loop, and took no row lock; all four are fixed and the route now calls the service. (3) **`confirmReceiptMatch` moved to `receiptMatchConfirmService.ts` and takes an allocations ARRAY.** One journal posts for the FULL bank line; allocating less is allowed and leaves a real unapplied remainder, allocating more is refused. Both bank paths refuse a closed or missing fiscal period PRE-write, because `postJournalEntry` only raises after `createJournalEntry` has INSERTed the draft. **`pages/api/accounting/ar/receipt-match/confirm.ts` must keep `validateBankReceiptApplication` and `confirmReceiptMatch` in SEPARATE try blocks**: the widened service calls `planReceiptApplication` a second time post-write as a race guard, throwing the same message shapes the route's old regex matched, so a race returned 400 and `withAuth` COMMITTED the posted journal. Only the pre-write half may be caught. (4) **`list_unapplied_receipts` splits the total by origin** — `agent` / `system` / `notStampedAsAgent` / `noJournal`. A receipt with no journal is its OWN bucket, and the human bucket is never called human: `createJournalEntry` stamps `human:<userId>` whenever a caller omits the meta.
